page: OVHcloud c2-7 is a Compute Optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, utilizing an Intel Haswell processor operating at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 7.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.5 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 50 GB of local SSD storage. It does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance sits in the lower tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks register in the bottom 10%, reflecting the older Haswell architecture. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 175.64 GB/sec, which drops to 20.03 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Similarly, database operations and redis SET performance fall into the bottom 25%, with redis achieving 2.71 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c2-7 offers a dedicated hardware allocation with no hyperthreading at an entry-level resource density. This makes it a predictable option for workloads requiring dedicated CPU cycles without the risk of noisy-neighbor resource contention, despite its modest absolute performance.

This server is suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale database operations, simple text processing, and running small language model inference tasks, where text generation for a 135M model reaches an average speed of 74.86 tokens per second.
description: OVHcloud c2-7 is a KVM-based, compute-optimized virtual server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Haswell architecture running at 3.0 GHz. It is equipped with 7.0 GB of RAM, 50 GB of local SSD storage, and no GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its compute and memory performance in the lower tiers, with stress-ng and Geekbench scores falling in the bottom 10% to 25% range. However, it maintains dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, ensuring consistent CPU allocation. This instance is best suited for lightweight, predictable workloads such as basic web serving, small-scale database operations, and simple text processing tasks.
